items.statement: Carry out acceptance testing of potable water used as a component whenever it comes from a source that does not control water quality to EPA standards.
items.quote: no acceptance testing is required for potable water unless it is obtained from sources that do not control water quality to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards
items.condition: source not controlled to EPA standards

items.statement: Do not use potable water to prepare USP dosage form drug products.
items.quote: potable water may not be used to prepare USP dosage form drug products

items.statement: Do not use potable water for laboratory reagents used to test solutions.
items.quote: potable water may not be used to prepare USP dosage form drug products or for laboratory reagents to test solutions

items.statement: Potable water may be used in the manufacture of drug substances (bulk drugs or bulk pharmaceutical chemicals).
items.quote: potable water may be used to manufacture drug substances (also known as bulk drugs or bulk pharmaceutical chemicals)

items.statement: Know the source of water used for wet granulation, for any aqueous liquid preparation and for the laboratory, and ensure that water is of USP purified water quality both chemically and microbiologically.
items.quote: determine the source of the water used for wet granulations or for any aqueous liquid preparations as well as for the laboratory. It should be of USP purified water quality both chemically and microbiologically.
items.condition: water for wet granulation, aqueous liquids or the laboratory

items.statement: Ensure there are no cross-connections between non-potable water lines and the potable water supply.
items.quote: Look carefully for any cross-connections to the potable water supply.

items.statement: Clearly label non-potable water supply lines as non-potable, especially where they are next to potable water supply connections.
items.quote: Non-potable water supply lines should be clearly marked as such, especially when adjacent to potable water supply connections.
items.condition: especially when adjacent to potable connections

items.statement: Produce USP water for injection only by distillation or reverse osmosis.
items.quote: USP WFI may be made only by distillation or reverse osmosis.

items.statement: Sample water at the point of use, after it has passed through the piping system, to detect contamination from piping defects.
items.quote: point-of-use sampling is indicated, that is, drawing the water sample after it has passed through the piping system

items.statement: Pay particular attention to deionized water systems because of the health risks of contaminated water, especially at small, less sophisticated manufacturers.
items.quote: Because of the potential health risks involved with the use of contaminated water, particular attention should be paid to deionized (DI) water systems, especially at small, less sophisticated manufacturers.
items.condition: especially at small, less sophisticated manufacturers

items.statement: Equip pharmaceutical water systems with corrective facilities to minimize contamination, such as access for sanitization or steam introduction, chlorinators, storage at elevated temperatures and filtration.
items.quote: the USP notes that water systems for pharmaceutical manufacturing should have "corrective facilities." By this they mean access to the system for sanitization or introduction of steam, chlorinators, storage at elevated temperatures, filtration, etc. Inquire about these during your inspection.

items.statement: Monitor source water microbial content often enough to capture fluctuations caused by seasonal changes in temperature and flora growth.
items.quote: Seasonal variations in temperature and growth of flora may also cause fluctuations in microbial content of source water. Monitoring should be frequent enough to cover these variations.

items.statement: Validate the operation of sand bed filter systems, with or without chlorination, together with any treatment that follows them.
items.quote: The operations of these systems should be validated along with any subsequent treatment.

items.statement: Where water storage tanks are used, know their capacity and rate of use and define how often their internal surfaces are flushed and sanitized.
items.quote: If storage tanks are used, determine the capacity, the rate of use, the frequency of flushing and sanitizing the internal surfaces.

items.statement: Do not rely on final filtration as the only treatment for purifying water.
items.quote: final filtration as the sole treatment for water purification is generally not acceptable

items.statement: Filtration may be acceptable in some cases, for example to reduce microbial or particulate loads in potable water used as an ingredient in chemical manufacturing where the water need not be sterile.
items.quote: However, filtration could be acceptable, for example, when used for reducing microbial/particulate loads in potable water used as an ingredient in chemical manufacturing where water need not be sterile.

items.statement: Where potable water is treated by chlorination, reach at least 0.2 mg per liter of free chlorine for the treatment to be effective.
items.quote: Chlorination of potable water is an effective treatment if minimum levels of 0.2mg/liter of free chlorine are attained.

items.statement: Maintaining continuously circulating WFI at 80 degrees C is acceptable.
items.quote: A temperature of 80^oC is commonly used and is acceptable.

items.statement: A circulating WFI temperature somewhat lower than 80 degrees C may be used only if the firm has adequate data showing the lower temperature works as intended.
items.quote: Somewhat lower temperatures may also be acceptable, provided the firm has adequate data to demonstrate that a lower temperature works as intended.

items.statement: If WFI is held at ambient temperature instead of recirculating at elevated temperature, discard it or divert it to non-WFI use 24 hours after it is produced.
items.quote: If WFI is held at ambient temperature rather than recirculation at elevated temperature, it must be dumped or diverted to non-WFI use 24 hours after being produced.

items.statement: Establish and monitor appropriate microbial specifications for water, even though no absolute microbial standards exist for water not intended to be sterile.
items.quote: Although there are no absolute microbial standards for water (other than water intended to be sterile), the CGMP regulations require that appropriate specifications be established and monitored.

items.statement: Base the water specification on the intended use of the water.
items.quote: The specification must take into account the intended use of the water

items.statement: Water used to formulate a product should contain no organisms capable of growing in that product.
items.quote: water used to formulate a product should contain no organisms capable of growing in the product
items.condition: water used to formulate a product

items.statement: Base water action or alert limits on validation data and set them low enough to signal significant changes from normal operating conditions.
items.quote: Action or alert limits must be based upon validation data and must be set low enough to signal significant changes from normal operating conditions.
